research.title: Attention-centered Generative User Interfaces for All

research.title: Human attention and its implications for human–computer interaction

candidates.title: Focus Rearranges the Room
candidates.reason: Makes attention a reversible spatial transformation while preserving every contextual cue.

candidates.title: The Interruption Door
candidates.reason: Strong architectural metaphor, but opening panels resembles familiar navigation.

candidates.title: Peripheral Sentence
candidates.reason: Useful attention model with less dramatic spatial consequence.

candidates.title: Return Path
candidates.reason: Excellent resumption premise, though closer to a productivity interface.

candidates.title: A Window Interrupts
candidates.reason: Clear occlusion study but risks looking like modal UI.

candidates.title: Context Has Walls
candidates.reason: Spatially strong but the content hierarchy is less immediately operable.

candidates.title: Six Ways Back
candidates.reason: Good keyboard structure with an overly literal navigation metaphor.

candidates.title: The Center Is Temporary
candidates.reason: Conceptually precise, but weaker as an interaction instruction.

candidates.title: Attention Without Capture
candidates.reason: Ethically meaningful, yet difficult to embody without explanatory copy.

candidates.title: Resume Here
candidates.reason: Strong accessibility principle with insufficient visual transformation.

hypothesis: Can an interface make focus spatially powerful without hiding or destroying its context?
interaction: Choose one of six thoughts by tap, click, Tab, or arrow keys. The selected thought occupies the visual center while all others remain legible as surrounding context.
performance: No external assets, fonts, timers, animation frames, audio, or storage; transformations use CSS only.
self_critique: The room metaphor is visually clear, but the six authored thoughts constrain exploration; future spatial work should let content structure emerge from visitor input without becoming a generic canvas.
